narrative.intro: Flightsafety Defense holds $665M in federal contract obligations for FY2026 to date. Flightsafety Defense received 6 awards this fiscal year, with an average award size of $111M, and obligations are up 778.1% year over year. Flightsafety Defense shows a sharp step-up from prior years: obligations were $78.9M in FY21, $74.2M in FY22, $99.7M in FY23, $81.3M in FY24, and $75.7M in FY25. Flightsafety Defense concentrates work in two markets so far this year: Other Aircraft Parts and Auxiliary Equipment Manufacturing at $641M, and Flight Training at $23.8M. Flightsafety Defense’s FY2026 totals are partial, covering the fiscal year to date, while the largest-awards and expiring-contracts tables report total contract values rather than current-year obligations. Flightsafety Defense’s current profile reflects a small number of large awards driving most obligations, and the NAICS mix indicates a focus on aircraft parts and training services rather than a broad spread across many industries.
